content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost rebalance lifts service level to 88.8% for 13:15-15:30 against the 80% target","why":"A sick wave has removed staff on both queues: 8 payments and 12 general agents are off sick against usual levels of 2.6 and 2.4, and payments had 26 agents on at 13:00 versus 34 planned. Call volume is below forecast (payments -2.7%, general -7.6%), so this is a staffing gap, not a demand spike. Doing nothing is predicted to reach 84.8%, but payments would sit at 81.0%, only just above target. P1 delays payments breaks 13:15-14:15 by 30 minutes and moves 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 13:15-14:00. It also moves 2 back from payments to general 19:00-20:00. This lifts payments to 85.2% and general to 93.6%, and cuts abandons from 3.0% to 1.8%. It costs nothing and breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["P2 and P3 add overtime for 4 payments agents at INR 720 but gain at most 0.8 points (89.6% / 89.5%), and P2 has a slightly higher abandon rate (2.0%). The extra spend isn't justified.","P0 costs nothing but leaves payments at 81.0% with 3.0% abandons, a thin margin if more sickness is reported.","General is not put at risk: lending it 2 agents still leaves it at 93.6%, and rest-of-day service level improves from 91.0% to 92.9%."],"watch":"Check for any further sick calls on payments. P1's payments margin is 85.2% against an 80% target, so if more agents drop out, move to the overtime option (P3, INR 720). Make sure the delayed breaks are actually taken once the 13:15-14:15 window ends."}
